stem: A university's platform team needs an Application Load Balancer's certificate to renew itself automatically with no manual steps, and separately needs a certificate on a self-managed EC2 web server that ACM does not directly integrate with, also renewed automatically. Which TWO approaches meet these two goals? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Import a third-party certificate into ACM and attach it to the Application Load Balancer
Request a DNS-validated ACM certificate and attach it to the Application Load Balancer
Attach the ACME-issued certificate directly to the Application Load Balancer instead of the EC2 host
Run a standard ACME client on the EC2 web server against ACM's ACME endpoint
Manually re-import a renewed certificate to the EC2 host every 90 days

rationale: A DNS-validated ACM certificate attached to an integrated service such as an Application Load Balancer is eligible for ACM's automatic managed renewal, with nothing to schedule. ACM's ACME protocol support lets a standard ACME client automate issuance and renewal directly on infrastructure outside ACM's integrated services, such as this self-managed EC2 web server. An imported third-party certificate is never eligible for managed renewal, so it still requires the team to track its expiration and replace it manually. ACME-issued certificates cannot be attached to Elastic Load Balancing, CloudFront, or API Gateway, so attaching one to the Application Load Balancer is not possible. Manually re-importing a certificate every 90 days is exactly the scheduled manual work the requirement rules out.
